findings.reason: the mechanism's exit condition must be pinned to the remote-tracking ref (as §2's "ancestor of the remote branch" is), or the skip silently re-arms the failure it was added to prevent.
findings.text: §5 makes `crew gc`'s live-pointer reap skip a pointer "until its head is on the branch" but never says which branch the ancestry test reads; `_is_ancestor` against the checkout's own HEAD is an ancestor check on local `main`, so a run whose head the coordinator merged locally and failed to push would have its kept pointer reaped by gc, leaving the ledger reading landed work the remote does not carry — the exact state §2 and this plan's own summary define as the defect

findings.reason: the plan's own definition of a landing is the remote, so the arm that removes the handle must be paired with one that keeps it when only the local branch moved.
findings.text: §5's second case stops at a successful `crew merge --run` leaving no live pointer, with no arm for a land whose fast-forward succeeded and whose push did not (`land_merge` raises `MergePushOutstandingError` at `reckon/crew/merge.py:808`, after the fast-forward has already moved the branch); a worker that unlinks the pointer whenever `land_merge` has touched the branch passes the gate while the head is not on the remote

findings.reason: the chosen mechanism (`crew_merge` retires the pointer after the land) is unaffected and the gc skip is still needed; only the rationale's "every" overstates an existing escape hatch the section could equally have used.
findings.text: the claim that `pending_landing.finish_pending_landings` "skips every run whose pointer is still live" is not exact: the skip at `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:233` is `if run_id in live and not (pointer or {}).get("pending_landing_repair")`, so a live pointer marked `pending_landing_repair` is processed

response_events.note: §5's gc skip now reads the remote primary branch (origin/<primary> after a fetch), never local main

reasoning-1.note: §5's gc skip now reads the remote primary branch (origin/<primary> after a fetch), never local main
